newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 1996 current a/c surplus hits record.
newsitem.headline: French 1996 current a/c surplus hits record.

text.p: France racked up a seasonally adjusted current account surplus of 2.43 billion francs in December, pushing the total surplus for 1996 to a record 101 billion francs, the finance ministry said on Friday.
The total was up from a 69.97 billion franc surplus the previous year and represented 1.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The ministry said that this current account surplus to GDP ratio had only been exceeded once in the past 30 years -- in 1978.
"This is the fifth straight annual surplus since 1992, bearing witness to the structural nature of the recovery of our external trade," the ministry said in a statement.
Last month, France announced a record 1996 trade surplus of 122 billion francs and called the performance further proof of economy recovery and competitiveness.
